memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And God said, "Let there be lights in the vault of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark sacred times, and days and years, and let them be lights in the vault of the sky to give light on the earth." And it was so. - Gen 1:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
I've combined these two verses, as they form one complete command of God.

On the fourth day, God turns His attention to the skies and calls forth lights, to separate day from night, to mark seasons, days, and years, and to shine light upon the earth. Notice that God gives them purpose before they even appear. Nothing in creation is random. Everything God makes has a role assigned by His wisdom.

Think of what this means. The sun that warms your face, the moon that lights the night, the stars that fill the sky, all of them are servants, doing exactly what God appointed them to do. They mark our calendars, guide our seasons, and order our lives, all under His command.

This tells us that our God is a God of purpose and order, right down to the movement of the heavens. And if He assigns purpose to lights in the sky, how much more to you, made in His image? You are not drifting through life without meaning. God has good purposes prepared for you (Eph 2:10).

The heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 19:1). Tonight, if you can, look up. Let the faithful sun, moon, and stars remind you that the God who orders the skies is ordering your days as well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God has assigned real purpose to your life, as He did to the stars?
2. When did you last pause to let creation turn your heart towards its Maker?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You set the lights in the sky with purpose and order. Thank You that my life too has purpose in Your hands. Help me trust Your ordering of my days. Amen.
